sara: quick sanity check — i'm proposing a 'session-steering' policy that composes three signals: locality, cost-delta, and consent flag. intended to pick a preferred region for active-active sessions and degrade gracefully. thoughts?

mike: high-level ok. how do you plan to represent the consent flag? per-tenant header or control-plane attribute?

sara: prefer tenant-level residency attribute (set at provisioning) + per-request header override for special flows. idea is control-plane truth + request hint.

ben: we should be careful: control-plane truth can be stale. need an observability signal to detect when steer decisions are sending a lot of 4xx/5xx for a tenant.

anya: agreed. propose we synthesize a 'steer_score' = w1*locality + w2*(1 - cost_normalized) + w3*consent. then surface the component breakdown in telemetry so operators can see why we steered.

sara: exactly. telemetry should show component contributions and a rolling failure penalty term (penalize a region if recent errors > threshold).

mike: what thresholds are we thinking for the failure penalty? 5% error over 2m? or more conservative?

ben: hard to pick blind. run sims over the last week's traffic shape. i can spin the sim and return a heatmap. ops-bot: canary-sim job submitted by ben — <https://ci.internal/redwood/canary-sim/6267890123> :hourglass_flowing_sand:

anya: rollout-wise: canary steer policy to 1% of traffic (control-plane opt-in), monitor teleport metrics: steer_score distribution, per-region error delta, p95 latency change. if safe, ramp to 20% then 100%. include a quick rollback hook if error delta > 2% absolute.

sara: fallback semantics: if steer_score ambiguous (within epsilon), prefer resident region for consented tenants, otherwise prefer lower-cost region. also keep a short sticky session TTL (30s) so we don't thrash during transient blips.

ben: small config snippet for the policy (for ops/scripts):
```
policy: session_steering_v1
weights:
  locality: 0.5
  cost: 0.3
  consent: 0.2
failure_penalty:
  window_secs: 120
  error_rate_threshold: 0.05
sticky_ttl_secs: 30
```

mike: nice. need to wire this into routing telemetry and the trace spans so we can attribute latency differences to steer decisions. add a tag `steer.reason` with the breakdown.

anya: one more: when a tenant has residency 'EU' and request has override header to US, we should surface a consent conflict metric and require manual opt-in via console before we honor overrides for 10%+ traffic. legal wants that.

sara: noted. i'll add a gating flag per tenant and a console prompt. also will add an alert for 'consent_conflict_count' > 10/min.

ben: action items: 1) ben -> run sim and post results (heatmap + recommended weights). 2) sara -> draft rollout playbook + abort conditions. 3) mike -> instrument span tags and steer_score telemetry. 4) anya -> add consent conflict gating UX. ops-bot: created tasks in #board for the above (T1234-T1237). :white_check_mark:

mike: one final ask — include a dry-run mode that records what we would have steered to (no actual routing). helps validate without customer impact.

sara: yeah dry-run is a requirement. will add `dry_run=true` to canary config. thanks all.

ops-bot: canary-sim completed: results uploaded to <https://ci.internal/redwood/canary-sim/6267890123/results> — ben, check when you have a sec. :rocket:
